evidence.claim: Capital One's policy describes how it collects, uses and shares information when you use its websites, mobile applications and other online services.
Capital One says resettable mobile advertising IDs, like cookies and pixel tags, let it and its service providers identify your device over time for advertising purposes.
Capital One says it and third-party providers use online tracking technologies for data analytics, auditing, measurement, research, reporting and debugging, and to measure advertising effectiveness.
Users can opt out of some targeted advertising via industry opt-out pages or device privacy settings (Limit Ad Tracking on iOS, Opt out of Ads Personalization on Android).
Capital One says personal information is retained as long as reasonably necessary for the policy's purposes and consistent with its retention policies and applicable law.
Capital One says resettable advertising IDs and tracking technologies may be used for advertising and analytics, with opt-outs available via industry pages and device settings.

Exodus Privacy static analysis of version 6.12.4 (report dated Sept. 6, 2024) found code signatures for 4 known tracker SDK(s): Google AdMob (advertisement), Google CrashLytics (crash reporting), Google Firebase Analytics (analytics), New Relic (analytics). A signature shows the SDK is present, not what data it sends.
